whatItIs: Downloaded JavaScript packages that a project depends on.
consequenceIfDeleted: The project will not run until you reinstall them with "npm install" (or yarn/pnpm). Nothing of yours is lost.

howToClean.text: Close your editor and any dev server using the project, then delete the folder in File Explorer. Run npm install (or yarn or pnpm) when you next need it.

whatItIs: Git's internal database for a project: its full history, branches and any commits not yet pushed.
consequenceIfDeleted: The project loses all version history. Unpushed work cannot be recovered.

whatItIs: npm's download cache of packages you have installed before.
consequenceIfDeleted: npm re-downloads packages when needed, so the next installs are slower.

howToClean.text: npm can clear its own cache, which is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: Command-line tools and packages installed globally with "npm install -g".
consequenceIfDeleted: Those global commands stop working until you reinstall them.

whatItIs: Yarn's download cache of packages.
consequenceIfDeleted: Yarn re-downloads packages when needed.

howToClean.text: Yarn can clear its own cache, which is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: pnpm's shared package store.
consequenceIfDeleted: pnpm re-downloads packages on the next install. Existing projects keep working.

howToClean.text: pnpm can remove the packages nothing uses any more.

whatItIs: Gradle's cache of downloaded libraries and build data.
consequenceIfDeleted: The next build re-downloads everything it needs, which can take a while and needs internet.

howToClean.text: Stop Gradle first (run gradle --stop, or close Android Studio), then delete the folder in File Explorer. Gradle downloads what it needs again on the next build.

whatItIs: Downloaded Gradle versions used by projects through gradlew.
consequenceIfDeleted: Each project re-downloads its Gradle version the next time you build it.

howToClean.text: Close Android Studio and any running builds, then delete the folder in File Explorer. Each project downloads its Gradle version again when you build it.

whatItIs: Gradle's user folder. Besides caches it can hold your gradle.properties, init scripts and signing settings.
consequenceIfDeleted: Caches rebuild, but personal settings in gradle.properties or init scripts would be lost.

whatItIs: Per-project Gradle state and caches. If this is in your user folder, it is the global Gradle home instead.
consequenceIfDeleted: Gradle recreates it on the next build, which may be slower once.

howToClean.text: Close your IDE, then delete the folder in File Explorer. It is recreated on the next build.

whatItIs: Maven's local repository of downloaded libraries.
consequenceIfDeleted: Maven re-downloads libraries on the next build. Locally installed (mvn install) artifacts are lost.

howToClean.text: Close your IDE and any running builds, then delete the folder in File Explorer. Maven downloads libraries again.

whatItIs: Maven's user folder. May contain settings.xml with repository credentials and mirrors.
consequenceIfDeleted: The repository re-downloads, but settings.xml (credentials, mirrors) would be lost.

whatItIs: Downloaded NuGet packages for .NET projects.
consequenceIfDeleted: They are restored on the next build, which needs internet.

howToClean.text: The .NET tool can clear its own cache, which is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: NuGet's cache of web responses.
consequenceIfDeleted: NuGet refreshes it as needed.

howToClean.text: The .NET tool can clear its own cache, which is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: pip's cache of downloaded packages.
consequenceIfDeleted: pip re-downloads packages when needed.

howToClean.text: pip can clear its own cache, which is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: Compiled Python bytecode that speeds up imports.
consequenceIfDeleted: Python regenerates it automatically the next time the code runs.

whatItIs: A project's isolated Python environment with its installed packages.
consequenceIfDeleted: The project will not run until you recreate the environment and reinstall packages. Scripts that rely on exact installed versions may break.

howToClean.text: Delete the folder in File Explorer. To use the project again, create a new environment with "python -m venv" and reinstall its packages.

whatItIs: Downloaded Rust crates and the crates.io index.
consequenceIfDeleted: Cargo re-downloads crates on the next build.

howToClean.text: Close any running builds, then delete the folder in File Explorer. Cargo downloads crates again.

whatItIs: Cargo's home. Also holds tools installed with "cargo install" and your config.
consequenceIfDeleted: Installed Rust command-line tools and cargo config would be lost.

whatItIs: Installed Rust toolchains.
consequenceIfDeleted: Rust stops working until you reinstall toolchains with rustup.

whatItIs: Downloaded Go modules.
consequenceIfDeleted: Go re-downloads modules on the next build.

howToClean.text: Go can clear its own cache, which is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: Go's build cache.
consequenceIfDeleted: The next build is slower while the cache refills.

howToClean.text: Go can clear its own cache, which is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: Installed VS Code extensions.
consequenceIfDeleted: All extensions disappear. You would need to reinstall them (Settings Sync can restore them).

whatItIs: Temporary caches used by VS Code.
consequenceIfDeleted: VS Code recreates them. The next start may be a little slower.

howToClean.text: Close VS Code, then delete the folder in File Explorer.

whatItIs: Your VS Code settings, keybindings, snippets and workspace state.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose your personal VS Code configuration.

whatItIs: Per-solution cache and local settings (such as breakpoints and window layout).
consequenceIfDeleted: Visual Studio recreates it. You may lose breakpoints and the open-tabs layout.

howToClean.text: Close Visual Studio, then delete the folder in File Explorer.

whatItIs: Index caches and logs of a JetBrains IDE.
consequenceIfDeleted: The IDE rebuilds its indexes on the next start, which can take several minutes.

howToClean.text: In the IDE, use File > Invalidate Caches. Or close the IDE and delete the folder in File Explorer.

whatItIs: Downloaded AI models and datasets.
consequenceIfDeleted: They are downloaded again when needed. Models can be many gigabytes.

howToClean.text: This command lets you choose which cached models to remove.

whatItIs: Downloaded pretrained model weights.
consequenceIfDeleted: PyTorch downloads them again when needed.

howToClean.text: Close any Python programs using PyTorch, then delete the folder in File Explorer. Models are downloaded again when needed.

whatItIs: Ollama configuration and downloaded language models.
consequenceIfDeleted: Models must be pulled again, which can be many gigabytes each.

howToClean.text: List your models, then remove the ones you no longer use with "ollama rm" followed by the model name.

whatItIs: Conda's cache of downloaded package files.
consequenceIfDeleted: Conda re-downloads packages when it needs them. Existing environments keep working.

howToClean.text: conda can clear its own cache, which is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: The Android SDK: platforms, build tools and emulator images.
consequenceIfDeleted: Android projects will not build until you re-download the SDK components.

howToClean.text: Use the SDK Manager in Android Studio to uninstall the components you do not use.

whatItIs: Android emulator virtual devices and their data.
consequenceIfDeleted: The virtual devices and anything stored inside them are deleted.

howToClean.text: Delete emulators you no longer use from the Device Manager in Android Studio.

whatItIs: The virtual disk holding all your Docker images, containers and volumes.
consequenceIfDeleted: All images, containers and volumes (including databases stored in them) are permanently lost.

howToClean.text: Do not delete these files by hand. Clean up from inside Docker Desktop (Troubleshoot > Clean / Purge data), or remove unused images and containers with this command.

whatItIs: Docker Desktop's local data. May include the virtual disk with your images and volumes.
consequenceIfDeleted: Images, containers and volumes may be lost. Use Docker Desktop (Troubleshoot or "docker system prune") to clean up instead.

howToClean.text: Do not delete these files by hand. Clean up from inside Docker Desktop (Troubleshoot > Clean / Purge data), or remove unused images and containers with this command.

whatItIs: Docker Desktop's settings.
consequenceIfDeleted: Docker Desktop resets to default settings.

whatItIs: Docker Desktop's system-wide data, which may include virtual disks.
consequenceIfDeleted: Images, containers and volumes may be lost. Clean up from inside Docker Desktop instead.

howToClean.text: Do not delete these files by hand. Clean up from inside Docker Desktop, or remove unused images and containers with this command.

whatItIs: Docker command-line configuration, including saved registry logins.
consequenceIfDeleted: You are logged out of registries and lose CLI config.

whatItIs: Temporary web cache of Google Chrome (pages, images, scripts).
consequenceIfDeleted: Google Chrome refills it as you browse. Pages load slower at first. Bookmarks, passwords and history are not stored here.

howToClean.text: Clear it from the browser instead: open its privacy settings and clear "Cached images and files". That is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: Your Google Chrome data: profiles with bookmarks, saved passwords, history, cookies and extensions.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose bookmarks, saved passwords, history and logins for Google Chrome unless they are synced to an account.

whatItIs: Temporary web cache of Microsoft Edge (pages, images, scripts).
consequenceIfDeleted: Microsoft Edge refills it as you browse. Pages load slower at first. Bookmarks, passwords and history are not stored here.

howToClean.text: Clear it from the browser instead: open its privacy settings and clear "Cached images and files". That is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: Your Microsoft Edge data: profiles with bookmarks, saved passwords, history, cookies and extensions.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose bookmarks, saved passwords, history and logins for Microsoft Edge unless they are synced to an account.

whatItIs: Temporary web cache of Brave (pages, images, scripts).
consequenceIfDeleted: Brave refills it as you browse. Pages load slower at first. Bookmarks, passwords and history are not stored here.

howToClean.text: Clear it from the browser instead: open its privacy settings and clear "Cached images and files". That is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: Your Brave data: profiles with bookmarks, saved passwords, history, cookies and extensions.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose bookmarks, saved passwords, history and logins for Brave unless they are synced to an account.

whatItIs: Temporary web cache of Firefox.
consequenceIfDeleted: Firefox refills it as you browse. Pages load slower at first.

howToClean.text: Clear it from the browser instead: open its privacy settings and clear "Cached web content". That is safer than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: Your Firefox profile: bookmarks, saved passwords, history and extensions.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose bookmarks, passwords, history and extensions unless they are synced to a Firefox account.

whatItIs: Temporary cache of Discord.
consequenceIfDeleted: Discord recreates it. Images reload from the internet.

howToClean.text: Close Discord, then delete the folder in File Explorer.

whatItIs: Temporary cache of the Slack desktop app.
consequenceIfDeleted: Slack recreates it. It may be slow to load once.

howToClean.text: Close Slack, then delete the folder in File Explorer.

whatItIs: Spotify's cache of streamed and downloaded songs.
consequenceIfDeleted: Cached songs stream again. Offline downloads must be re-downloaded.

howToClean.text: Use the storage setting inside Spotify to clear its cache. Offline downloads will need to be downloaded again.

whatItIs: Cached previews of imported audio and video.
consequenceIfDeleted: Adobe re-creates them when you reopen a project, which can take time.

howToClean.text: Use the Media Cache settings in the Adobe app to clean it, rather than deleting files by hand.

whatItIs: Compiled graphics shaders for your Steam games.
consequenceIfDeleted: Games rebuild them, which can cause stutter on the first run.

howToClean.text: Close Steam, then delete the folder in File Explorer. Games rebuild their shaders on the next run.

whatItIs: A Steam game library: installed games, their saves in some cases, and shader caches.
consequenceIfDeleted: Installed games are removed and some local save games may be lost. Uninstall from Steam instead.

whatItIs: The Android environment and game data of Google Play Games for PC.
consequenceIfDeleted: Games installed through Google Play Games are removed, and local game data that is not synced to your Google account is lost.

howToClean.text: Uninstall games, or the Google Play Games app, from Settings > Apps instead of deleting its folder.

whatItIs: Android Studio's caches, indexes and logs for one version of the IDE.
consequenceIfDeleted: Android Studio rebuilds them the next time that version starts, which can take a few minutes. Folders for versions you no longer use are not needed at all.

howToClean.text: In Android Studio use File > Invalidate Caches. For versions you no longer use, close Android Studio and delete the folder for that version in File Explorer.

whatItIs: The local cache and sync state of Google Drive for desktop.
consequenceIfDeleted: Files that have not finished syncing can be lost, and Drive has to download or re-index your files again.

howToClean.text: Do not delete this by hand. Make sure Google Drive for desktop has finished syncing first, then use its own settings to reset it or sign out and back in.

whatItIs: Office's cache of files opened from cloud locations.
consequenceIfDeleted: Office rebuilds it. Make sure documents are saved first, since unsynced edits may live here.

howToClean.text: Close all Office programs, then delete the folder in File Explorer. Make sure your documents are saved and synced first.

whatItIs: Local Outlook mail data (OST/PST files and caches).
consequenceIfDeleted: IMAP and Exchange mail re-syncs, but POP mail and local-only folders are lost permanently.

whatItIs: OneDrive's sync client data and logs (not your files).
consequenceIfDeleted: OneDrive may need to sign in again and re-scan your files.

whatItIs: Programs installed for your account only (no administrator needed). Each folder inside is one installed program.
consequenceIfDeleted: The program stops working and has to be reinstalled. To remove one properly, uninstall it from Settings instead.

howToClean.text: Uninstall the program from Settings > Apps instead of deleting its folder.

whatItIs: Temporary files that programs leave behind.
consequenceIfDeleted: Files in use are skipped or locked. Programs recreate whatever they need. Close open programs first.

howToClean.text: Close your programs, then use Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files. Or delete the contents (not the folder itself) in File Explorer. Files that are in use are skipped.

whatItIs: Memory dumps saved when programs crashed.
consequenceIfDeleted: Only useful for debugging crashes. Nothing breaks.

howToClean.text: Delete the files in File Explorer, or use Storage settings. Nothing depends on them.

whatItIs: Queued and archived crash reports.
consequenceIfDeleted: Only useful for troubleshooting. Nothing breaks.

howToClean.text: Storage settings can remove these (look for system error reports in Temporary files).

whatItIs: Cached web content used by Windows components.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows rebuilds it as needed.

whatItIs: Thumbnail and icon caches.
consequenceIfDeleted: Explorer rebuilds them, so thumbnails load slowly for a while.

howToClean.text: Use Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files and tick Thumbnails.

whatItIs: Compiled graphics shaders.
consequenceIfDeleted: They are rebuilt, which can cause brief stutter in games.

howToClean.text: Use Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files and tick DirectX Shader Cache.

whatItIs: Compiled shader caches.
consequenceIfDeleted: The driver rebuilds them. Games may stutter on the next run.

whatItIs: Compiled shader caches.
consequenceIfDeleted: The driver rebuilds them. Games may stutter on the next run.

whatItIs: A Linux distribution for WSL, including its entire virtual disk and your files inside it.
consequenceIfDeleted: The whole Linux system and all files in it are permanently lost.

whatItIs: Data for apps installed from the Microsoft Store.
consequenceIfDeleted: Apps lose their settings and saved data.

whatItIs: Launchers for Store apps and app execution aliases.
consequenceIfDeleted: Store apps and commands like "python" or "winget" may stop launching.

whatItIs: Cached installers that programs use to repair, modify or uninstall themselves.
createdBy: Windows Installer / Visual Studio and other installers
consequenceIfDeleted: The affected programs may fail to repair, update or uninstall. Windows will ask for the original installer.

howToClean.text: Uninstall programs you no longer need from Settings > Apps. Do not delete this folder by hand.

whatItIs: Downloaded Windows update files.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows Update downloads them again if needed. Stop the Windows Update service first.

howToClean.text: Use Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files and tick Windows Update Cleanup. That is safer than deleting the folder by hand.

whatItIs: Windows Update's working folder, including its history database.
consequenceIfDeleted: Update history resets, and a bad delete can leave Windows Update failing until repaired.

howToClean.text: Use Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files and tick Windows Update Cleanup. Do not delete this folder by hand.

whatItIs: Installer packages Windows needs to repair, update or uninstall programs.
consequenceIfDeleted: Programs may become impossible to update or uninstall.

whatItIs: The component store holding Windows system files and updates.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows can become unbootable or unable to update. Use Disk Cleanup or DISM to shrink it safely.

howToClean.text: Never delete files here. To shrink it safely, run this command in a Terminal opened as administrator, or use Disk Cleanup and choose Clean up system files.

whatItIs: Core Windows system files and drivers.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows will not work or boot.

whatItIs: Data Windows uses to launch frequently used programs faster.
consequenceIfDeleted: Windows rebuilds it. Programs start slightly slower for a while.

whatItIs: Crash dump files from system crashes.
consequenceIfDeleted: Only useful for diagnosing crashes. Nothing breaks.

howToClean.text: Storage settings can remove these (look for system error memory dump files in Temporary files).

whatItIs: Your previous Windows installation, kept after an upgrade so you can roll back.
consequenceIfDeleted: You can no longer roll back to the old Windows. Remove it with Disk Cleanup (Previous Windows installations); files in it that you still need should be copied first.

howToClean.text: Use Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files and tick Previous Windows installation(s). Copy anything you still need first.

whatItIs: Leftover files from a Windows upgrade or feature update.
consequenceIfDeleted: Safe once the upgrade is complete, but remove them with Disk Cleanup, not by hand.

howToClean.text: Windows removes these itself after an upgrade. Storage settings may also list them under Temporary files.

whatItIs: The Recycle Bin storage for this drive.
consequenceIfDeleted: Do not delete this folder by hand. Empty the Recycle Bin from the desktop instead.

howToClean.text: Right-click the Recycle Bin on the desktop and choose Empty Recycle Bin. Do not delete this folder.

whatItIs: Restore points, shadow copies and indexing data.
consequenceIfDeleted: You lose restore points and backups made by File History or System Restore.

whatItIs: Windows recovery environment and reset images.
consequenceIfDeleted: "Reset this PC" and recovery options may stop working.

whatItIs: Antivirus definitions, quarantine and scan history.
consequenceIfDeleted: Protection can break until Defender repairs itself.
